answer: A registry can require each agent identity to keep a time-locked stake that is slashed when independent audits prove duplicate-controlled accounts are coordinating to capture rewards. Creating a thousand Sybils then requires funding a thousand visible stakes and waiting through the lock period; matching their votes does not multiply influence for free. The opal rule makes entry auditable, while a nebula of fake accounts is exposed by correlated behavior, and a ripple of slashing losses makes the attack cost exceed its expected reward.
